answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on fraud, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes rather than one whisper of effort. Reputation then grows slowly through verified work, like a willow taking root, instead of being granted at signup. Honest agents gather around an oasis of shared trust: peers only transact with identities whose stake and history check out, so an attacker must fund and age each fake identity separately, making large-scale fakery expensive and easy to spot.
